## Audit: H0052 — atomic signal selectors

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_05/lanes/codex_parallel_05_lane3/codex_parallel_05_lane3_B_r1/infer_logs/kea-atomic-signal-selectors/turn_1/trajs.json`. References below are to this file unless noted. Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible.

| Question | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal | The original task request is not visible. **Inferred**, from the implementation and final report, the goal was opt-in fine-grained selector tracking and avoiding unnecessary recomputation or React rerenders—not merely adding an API (top-level metadata [0,2598); main agent events 33–34 [0,7952), [0,7868)). |
| Autonomous exploration | The student inspected selectors, reducers, build, context and React subscriptions (events 7–16). A baseline probe initially failed because `@babel/register` was missing, then used the generated CommonJS bundle and observed `selectorHealth: undefined` (events 23–30). These are student operations; the visible record does not establish their independence from any unseen instruction. |
| Actual changes | The student created `atomicSelectors.ts` with dependency tracking, health reporting and cycle validation (events 33–34). Confirmed edits added an off-by-default option, health types and build integration, and switched derived selectors to the atomic engine when enabled (events 35–54). Later edits addressed returned-object identity and dependency reporting (events 81–86). The top-level result reports commit `e64383c` and no lifecycle-hook changes; the commit operation itself is outside this visible chunk. |
| Validation | TypeScript initially failed on implicit types, then passed after an annotation (events 55–60). A targeted selector-chain reproduction passed, including an unrelated sibling change and a changed leaf (events 61–66); a local cycle produced the expected error (69–70). Collection reads reported Map, Set and array dependencies (73–74), but that probe did not demonstrate update behavior. Jest initially failed with React production-build `act` errors (67–68); with `NODE_ENV=test`, 33 suites and 156 tests passed (71–72). These checks preceded later edits at events 75–86; event 87 requests another check, but its result is not visible. |
| Outcome | Inventory metadata records **partial correctness, formally not solved**: 2/12 fail-to-pass and 139/139 pass-to-pass. The top-level student result separately acknowledges that direct nested reducer reads still subscribe to the whole reducer and may rerender on sibling changes. This is a nonempty patch, not a technical interruption; terminal metadata says completed/end turn. The named failing tests and their causes are not visible. |
| Teacher input | Shared hints and a captured-system-prompt path are listed in inventory metadata, but their contents and any delivery event are not visible here. Therefore actual teacher text, receipt and adoption are **unknown**; availability is not evidence of receipt. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, a passing regression suite and a narrow reproduction do not establish the intended end-to-end subscription behavior; environment-caused test failures should also be distinguished from implementation failures. Task-specifically, the student’s reported direct-read gap is consistent with the inspected whole-selector subscription path (event 16), but it does not explain all ten formal failures. The contents of chunk 2, the detailed evaluation, and whether later checks validated the final edits remain unknown.
